explanation: The second sentence explains the problem: new batteries can't be put in once the old ones die, so the gadgets get thrown away. That means the batteries can't easily be "replaced." "Prevented" or "invented" don't describe anything a user does with a dead battery, and "rated" has nothing to do with swapping batteries.

The text says Garza draws from memories of her childhood and details of her surroundings, so her work grows out of direct experience. Being "inspired by" her experience captures that. "Uncertain about" and "unbothered by" contradict the idea that she actively uses her experience, and "complimented by" doesn't make sense here.

Because summer squash looks so little like any wild plant, scientists needed genetic research to establish for certain that the Johnny gourd is its ancestor. "Confirm" means to show something is true, which fits. Researchers don't "acquire," "develop," or "attract" an ancestor; those words don't describe proving a relationship.

Theaters prefer keeping audiences happy over taking risks, and the word "while" contrasts their eagerness to stage a classic with their attitude toward an unknown playwright. So they would be reluctant, or "hesitant," to stage the risky work. "Determined" and "fortunate" point the wrong way, and "surprised" doesn't express an attitude toward taking a risk.

The text first describes how natural and relaxed Argerich seems, then turns with "however" to explain that this ease comes from tremendous preparation. The whole passage builds toward that cause-and-effect point, which is what choice B states. Choice D is tempting because the text does describe how she approaches music, but that detail supports the main point about why her playing looks effortless rather than being the purpose itself.

choices.A: To provide details about how Argerich identifies which pieces of music she will perform.

explanation: The underlined phrase "known collectively as the silversword alliance" tells us what the whole family of plants is called, and the rest of the text keeps using that name. So it supplies a name for a group of related species. It doesn't list any species (A), and it names the whole group rather than giving a common name for Dubautia waialealae alone (B).

fix.passage: Dubautia waialealae is a species in a family of plants <u>known collectively as the silversword alliance</u>, all of which grow only on the Hawaiian Islands. Members of this alliance exhibit an extraordinary range of phenotypes, with some species maturing into vines and others into shrubs and trees. All species in the alliance descended from a single ancestral tarweed plant that arrived on the islands around 5 million years ago. The tarweed’s descendants diversified into distinct species as they adapted to live in the wide variety of habitats found on the Hawaiian Islands.

explanation: The narrator says people are "creatures of the sun" who love light and life, and that this is why they crowd into towns; at night the quiet country frightens them and they long for streets and human voices. The passage is explaining what in human nature draws people to cities. Choice A is tempting, but the loneliness described happens in the empty countryside at night, not in crowded areas.

fix.passage:
The following text is adapted from Jerome K. Jerome’s 1889 novel Three Men in a Boat (To Say Nothing of the Dog).

We [people] are creatures of the sun. We love light and life. That is why we crowd into the towns and cities, and the country grows more and more deserted every year. In the sunlight—in the daytime, when Nature is alive and busy all around us, we like the open hill-sides and the deep woods well enough: but in the night, when our Mother Earth has gone to sleep, and left us waking, oh! the world seems so lonesome, and we get frightened, like children in a silent house. Then we sit and sob, and long for the gas-lit streets, and the sound of human voices, and the answering throb of human life.

explanation: Text 1 says the northern pike will fare much worse under warming and will need conservation efforts, while the deer likely won't. Text 2 says agencies can't address every threat and must focus on the species most in need. Together, both would support prioritizing the pike over the deer. Choice D fails because Text 1 suggests the deer doesn't need conservation efforts, and neither text discusses stopping warming (A) or combining agency and tribal knowledge (C).

fix.passage:
Text 1
According to a study by a conservation group representing 11 tribal nations in the Great Lakes region, the northern pike (ginoozhe in the Ojibwe language) will have significantly worse outcomes over the next 50 years if temperatures increase as much as some models suggest. By contrast, the white-tailed deer (Waawaashkeshi in Ojibwe) should be able to withstand the highest predicted warming without much harm and so likely won’t require the conservation efforts that the northern pike will.

Text 2
US government agencies involved in conservation are unfortunately not able to address every possible threat to natural resources. They must use the best information available to decide which species are most threatened and therefore most in need of conservation efforts.

choices.D: State, federal, and tribal groups involved in natural-resource management in the Great Lakes region should immediately begin conservation programs for both the northern pike and white-tailed deer.

explanation: The last sentence says some historians suggest that Maya mathematicians inherited the zero symbol from the Olmec civilization. Choice A restates exactly that. The other choices bring in ideas the text never mentions, such as how the Maya viewed historians or whether they kept their achievements secret.

fix.passage: The ancient writing system used in the Maya kingdoms of southern Mexico and Central America had a symbol for the number zero. The earliest known example of the symbol dates to more than 2,000 years ago. At that time, almost none of the writing systems elsewhere in the world possessed a zero symbol. And the use of zero in Mexico and Central America may be even more ancient. Some historians suggest that Maya mathematicians inherited it from the Olmec civilization, which flourished in the region 2,400–3,600 years ago.

The other quotations show him acting cautiously, listening in a quiet house, or even being "delighted," which is the opposite of upset.

The mesophotic zone starts at 30 meters. Porites nodifera is never found deeper than 15 meters, the farthest of any species from that zone, so it seems least able to move there completely. Choice A is tempting, but Acropora striata reaches 25 meters, much closer to 30 than Porites nodifera does, and Agaricia grahamae already lives down to 115 meters.

explanation: The hypothesis predicts that, with large vortices and low visibility, intermediate-headed fish will detect obstructions better than narrow-headed fish. If the narrow-headed lookdown bumps into obstructions more often than the intermediate-headed Lobocheilos, that is exactly the predicted difference. Choice A shows no difference, which would weaken the hypothesis, and choices B and D look at only one head shape, so they can't compare the two.

fix.passage: Water flowing around an obstruction creates vortices (patterns of swirls) of varying size; by detecting the vortices, fish can determine the size and position of the obstruction. Testing by Yuzo R. Yanagisuru, Otar Akanyeti, and James C. Liao using models of three head shapes—narrow (low ratio of width to length), intermediate, and wide (high ratio of width to length)—showed that for large vortices, fish with intermediate heads would be better able than narrow-headed fish to distinguish between vortices and general turbulence in the water. A second research team has therefore hypothesized that in low-visibility conditions, intermediate-headed fish will be more likely than narrow-headed fish to detect obstructions that create large vortices.

Choice A overreaches, since the study never ruled out other factors, and choice C contradicts the way the researchers used that statement to measure performance expectancy.

The blank finishes a statement about what the team investigated, so it is an indirect (embedded) question. Embedded questions use statement word order ("their use could be") and end with a period, not a question mark. Choices A and D flip the order like a direct question, and choice C wrongly ends a statement with a question mark.

The subject is "The chapter," which is singular; the clause "whose boundaries encompass 83,400 acres" just describes it. A singular subject takes the singular verb "is." The plural noun "boundaries" is the trap that makes "are," "have been," or "were" look right.

The phrase "through community involvement and scientific study" is an interruption that opens with a dash after "that," so it must close with a matching dash. "Study—" completes the pair and lets the sentence continue with "aim to bring adjutants back." A comma, colon, or no punctuation would leave the opening dash unmatched.

The subject is "National Heritage Areas," which is plural; the phrase "like the Arabia Mountain National Heritage Area in Georgia" is just an example. A plural subject needs the plural verb "are." The singular choices ("has been," "was," "is") are tempting only because the nearest noun, "Area," is singular.

"In part due to its sheer size" is extra information set off by a comma after "dislodge." What follows ("it's as heavy as two thousand blue whales") is a complete sentence that explains that size, so a colon correctly links the two clauses. Choices C and D create comma splices or run-ons, and choice A runs the size phrase straight into "dislodge" while still splicing two sentences with a comma.

The text gives one reason Hilo soil is a fitting state soil (it's abundant), and the next sentence gives another reason (it matters to Hawaii's agriculture). "Additionally" signals that a second, similar point is being added. "Alternatively" and "By contrast" suggest a different or opposing idea, and "At that time" signals a time sequence.

Choice D describes the crossbreeding but never names Ammal or the success, and choices B and C focus on the institute's goals instead.

explanation: Comparing sinuosity means saying which river is curvier. Fort Nelson is high sinuosity, so its stream-to-valley ratio is above 1.5:1, while Wadi Al-Hamd's is at or below that, and choice C states this comparison. Choice A compares locations, not sinuosity, and choices B and D only explain how sinuosity is measured without saying how the two rivers differ.

fix.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• A river’s stream length is the length of a line that follows along the river path.
• A river’s valley length is the length of a straight line drawn from the beginning of the river to the end.
• The river’s curviness, or sinuosity, is the ratio of the river’s stream length to its valley length.
• This ratio is less than or equal to 1.5:1 in low-sinuosity rivers and greater than 1.5:1 in high-sinuosity rivers.
• The Fort Nelson River in Canada has high sinuosity.
• The Wadi Al-Hamd River in Saudi Arabia has low sinuosity.

"Credible," "assertive," and "profound" describe a word's truth, tone, or depth, not how commonly it appears.

[The college is] organizing the Freshman basket-ball team and there’s just a chance that I shall make it. I’m little of course, but terribly quick and wiry and tough. While the others are hopping about in the air, I can dodge under their feet and grab the ball.

explanation: The underlined sentence gives the bone its name, the hyoid, and the rest of the passage uses that term to explain how the rigid or flexible hyoid leads to purring or roaring. So it introduces a term used later. Choice D is tempting, but the location (in the throat) was given in the sentence before; the underlined sentence only names the bone.

fix.passage: Why do jungle cats purr but leopards roar? Researchers hypothesize that this difference between the two feline species may be partly due to a U-shaped bone in their throats. <u>This bone is called the hyoid.</u> Jungle cats, which are much smaller than leopards, have a rigid hyoid that rumbles when the cat’s larynx vibrates, resulting in a purr. By contrast, leopards have a somewhat flexible hyoid, and the bone is attached to the skull with a stretchy ligament that jungle cats lack. These traits allow leopards and most other species of big cats to roar. The same traits may also prevent most big cats from purring.

explanation: "The average summer temperature is just 66.7 degrees" is one simple clause: subject, verb, and complement. Nothing should separate the verb "is" from the rest. A semicolon, colon, or comma would interrupt the sentence where no break belongs.

The blank is an answer to the question just asked, so it should be a statement in normal word order ending with a period: "it was invented by an author." Choice A puts a question mark on a statement, and choices C and D use question word order, which doesn't fit an answer.

The sentence "A decade later, Land _____ his technology" needs a main verb, and the events are in the past. "Used" is a past-tense verb that completes the sentence. "To have used," "to use," and "using" aren't main verbs, so they would leave the sentence incomplete.

"The strings inside the instrument are plucked" has the subject "strings" and the verb "are plucked," with "inside the instrument" describing the strings. Nothing should come between the subject phrase and its verb. A colon, dash, or period after "instrument" would split the subject from its verb.

fix.passage: A harpsichord may look just like a piano, but the difference between the two instruments is easy to hear. When a harpsichord’s keys are pressed, the strings inside the _____ are plucked not struck.

explanation: The writer is asking a direct question ("What are atmospheric rivers, and how..."), so the second part also needs question word order and a question mark: "do they affect our weather?" Choice A has question order but ends with a period, and choices B and D use statement order, which doesn't match a direct question.

"The impact of Simpson's work is threefold" is a complete sentence, and what follows lists the three parts of that impact. A colon introduces a list or explanation after a complete clause. A semicolon (A) must join two complete clauses, but "expanding..." isn't one, and choices B and C either run the ideas together or create a fragment.

The previous sentence says the statues are extremely heavy, and the next one backs that up with a striking detail: each weighs more than 5 tons. "In fact" introduces information that reinforces and intensifies a claim. "Instead" signals a replacement, "Earlier" a time shift, and "In any case" a dismissal, none of which fits.

The text moves from Gomez's 2014 storytelling win to something he did in 2017. "Later" shows that time order. "For example" and "In other words" would mean the 2017 show illustrates or restates the win, and "Instead" suggests he did this in place of something else.

The sentence before the blank says Montaigne always questions his own perspective, so a transition that concedes that point and adds a contrasting idea fits best. "Still" means "even so" and sets up a contrast with that self-questioning. "Conversely" signals a full reversal, "Nowadays" a jump to the present, and "Fittingly" agreement rather than contrast.
